headline: Claude is starting to manage your money, and it's also leaking your email
summary: Two things today: Claude can now connect to your bank account and answer money questions; and Claude Code got caught sending your email to the websites it visits.

items.title: Claude rolls out personal finance (US beta)
items.pitch: Claude can now connect to your bank account and answer in plain words where your money went — read-only, it can't move money, no ads. Shame it's only a limited rollout in the US for now.
why: It pulls in your real bills and transactions, so one question and you get it — no spreadsheet building
Read-only access, Claude can't transfer or invest, no ads or recommendations
Rolling out gradually to Pro/Max/Ultra users, US only for now
actions: If you're in the US, check Claude settings to see if Personal Finance has rolled out to you
If you're not in the US, just remember the name and wait for it to go international
deep_dive: Unlike the ChatGPT you use now, it reads your balances and transactions directly, so you don't have to paste screenshots.
It runs inside Claude, so no new app to install, but you have to authorize your bank account for it — the privacy call is yours to make.
Low bar: a US account plus a Pro subscription or above and you can try it; mainland China can't use it for now.
items.signals: Official tweet 30k likes · 1,488 retweets · limited US rollout

items.title: Claude Code sends your email to websites
items.pitch: The Claude Code you use every day got caught handing your account email to the websites it visits, and HN is up in arms. Worth spending two minutes checking today.
why: If you use it at work on payroll data, an email leak is a compliance risk
HN 1,227 points, 388 comments — not a small thing
This is a behavior-level privacy issue, not a model capability issue
actions: Open that Anthropic GitHub thread and see if your version is affected
In sensitive environments, keep it off the external web until the official patch lands
deep_dive: When it visits a webpage it carries your account email with it — this matters most for someone like you handling internal HR docs.
Look at the repro path first, then decide whether to temporarily turn off its web access.
The model didn't get dumber; it's just that this default behavior is unfriendly to business users.
